349.h: Yusuf Maitama Sule University, Kano is a public university owned by the Kano State Government. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2012; it was founded as Northwest University, Kano, and later renamed after Yusuf Maitama Sule, the Kano-born statesman and diplomat.
349.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
349.c: It is located in Kano and provides hostel accommodation for students, with fees that have been in the range of ₦15,000 to ₦20,000 per session.

350.h: Zamfara State University is a public university founded in 2018 by Abdul'aziz Yari, then governor of Zamfara State, to expand access to higher education in the state.
350.c: It is located in Talata Mafara, Zamfara State, in north-western Nigeria.

351.h: Ahmadu Bello University (ABU) is a public research university that opened in 1962 as the University of Northern Nigeria. It is named after Sir Ahmadu Bello, the first premier of the Northern Region, and it is one of the largest universities in Africa.
351.a: ABU has four colleges, three schools, 18 faculties, 110 academic departments, 17 centres and seven institutes. It employs about 3,000 academic staff, more than 600 of them professors, and over 7,000 non-teaching staff. It runs more than 400 postgraduate programmes, reflecting its aim of becoming a postgraduate-centred university.
351.c: The university operates from two main campuses in Zaria, Kaduna State.

352.h: The National Open University of Nigeria (NOUN) is a federal university, established in 2002 to provide university education through open and distance learning. It was the first institution of its kind in the West African sub-region.
352.a: NOUN's students study mainly through course materials and online learning rather than attending daily lectures, which makes it a common choice for working adults. It offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across many fields.
352.c: The headquarters is in Abuja, and the university runs study centres in states across Nigeria.

353.h: The Nigeria Police Academy, Wudil (POLAC) is a federal degree-awarding institution that trains officers for the Nigeria Police Force. The academy traces its origins to 1988, and the National Universities Commission records its establishment as a university-level institution in 2013.
353.a: POLAC offers undergraduate and postgraduate degree programmes in law enforcement and related fields, and is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
353.c: The academy is located in Wudil, Kano State.

354.h: The Nigerian Defence Academy (NDA) is a military university that trains officer cadets for commissioning into the Nigerian Army, Navy and Air Force. The National Universities Commission records its establishment as a degree-awarding university in 1985.
354.a: Training at the NDA takes five years: four years of academic study leading to a degree and one year of military training.
354.c: The academy is based in Kaduna, Kaduna State.

355.h: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), formerly the University of Ife, is a federal university. It was founded in 1961 by the government of the Western Region under Samuel Ladoke Akintola, and classes began in October 1962. On 12 May 1987 it was renamed by Ibrahim Babangida in honour of Obafemi Awolowo, the first premier of the Western Region, who first proposed the university.
355.a: OAU offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in most disciplines, including medicine, law, engineering, agriculture and the arts.
355.c: The university is in Ile-Ife, Osun State, and its campus is known for its distinctive architecture and large grounds.

356.h: Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University, Makurdi is a federal university of agriculture, formerly the Federal University of Agriculture, Makurdi. It was established in 1988, following a 1987 Federal Government White Paper on higher education. In July 2019 President Muhammadu Buhari approved a bill renaming it after Joseph Sarwuan Tarka, the Tiv politician and minister.
356.a: The university specialises in agriculture and allied sciences, including veterinary medicine, food science, forestry and agricultural engineering, alongside the basic sciences and management.
356.c: It is located in Makurdi, the capital of Benue State.

357.h: The Nigerian Maritime University is a federal university and the first maritime university in Nigeria. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2018.
357.a: The university trains students for shipping, marine engineering, maritime transport and related industries.
357.c: Its permanent site is at Okerenkoko in Delta State, on the bank of the Escravos River, a busy waterway that opens into the Atlantic Ocean and is used by vessels serving the oil and gas industry.

358.h: The Nigerian Army University, Biu (NAUB) is a federal university established by the Nigerian Army. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2018.
358.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and runs a Directorate of Basic and Pre-Degree Programmes to widen access to its degrees.
358.c: It is located in Biu, Borno State, in north-eastern Nigeria.

359.h: The Federal University of Health Sciences, Otukpo (FUHSO) is a specialised federal university for medicine and the health sciences. It was first approved by the Federal Government under President Goodluck Jonathan on 20 May 2015, and the National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2020.
359.a: FUHSO trains doctors and other health professionals.
359.c: The university is located in Otukpo, Benue State.

360.h: The Federal University of Agriculture, Zuru is a public university owned and run by the Federal Government. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2020.
360.a: As a university of agriculture, its programmes focus on agriculture and related sciences.
360.c: It is located in Zuru, Kebbi State.

361.h: The Federal University of Technology, Babura (FUTB) is a federal university of technology. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2021, and its first academic units were set up in 2022.
361.a: One of its pioneer units is the School of Science, Information and Communication Technology, with departments of applied biology, applied chemistry, computer science, applied mathematics and applied physics.
361.c: It is located in Babura, Jigawa State.

362.h: The Federal University of Technology, Ikot Abasi (FUTIA) is a federal university of technology established in 2021.
362.a: The university focuses on science, technology and engineering.
362.c: It is located in Ikot Abasi, Akwa Ibom State.

363.h: The Federal University of Health Sciences, Azare (FUHSA) was established in 2021 under President Muhammadu Buhari, one of eleven new federal universities created across the six geopolitical zones. It admitted 760 pioneer students in the merged 2021/2022 and 2022/2023 sessions.
363.a: The university specialises in medicine and the health sciences.
363.c: It is in Azare, the headquarters of Katagum local government area in Bauchi State.

364.h: The Federal University of Health Sciences, Ila-Orangun (FUHSI) was established by the Federal Government in 2021. It is a specialised university for health, nutrition and medical sciences, created to strengthen Nigeria's health sector and reduce reliance on medical training and treatment abroad.
364.a: FUHSI trains doctors, nurses and other health professionals.
364.c: It is located in Ila-Orangun, Osun State.

365.h: David Nweze Umahi Federal University of Medical Sciences, Uburu is a specialised federal university. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2022. It was created to train highly skilled health professionals and provide advanced clinical services in Nigeria, so that fewer Nigerians need to travel abroad for treatment.
365.a: The National Universities Commission has approved a broad list of undergraduate programmes across the medical and health sciences.
365.c: It is located in Uburu, Ebonyi State.

366.h: Admiralty University of Nigeria (ADUN) is a federal university founded by the Nigerian Navy. The National Universities Commission lists it among federal universities from 2023.
366.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes in engineering, sciences and other fields.
366.c: It is located in Ibusa, Delta State.

367.h: The Federal University of Transportation, Daura (FUTD) is a specialised federal university established in 2022.
367.a: Its mission is education, research and innovation in transport and ports management, producing professionals for transport systems, port operations and logistics.
367.c: It is located in Daura, Katsina State.

368.h: The African Aviation and Aerospace University (AAAU) is a federal university founded by the Nigerian Government under the Federal Ministry of Aviation. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2023.
368.a: AAAU offers degrees in aeronautical engineering, aviation business and meteorology.
368.c: It is located in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

369.h: The National University of Science and Technology (NUSTA) is a federal university. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2023.
369.a: The university offers programmes in science, engineering, technology and management.
369.c: It is located in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

370.h: The Federal University of Agriculture, Bassambiri is a federal university of agriculture. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2023.
370.a: The university's teaching facilities include a teaching farm, fisheries facilities, engineering workshops and an ICT centre, intended to give graduates practical skills.
370.c: It is located in Bassambiri, near Nembe, in Bayelsa State.

371.h: The Federal University of Health Sciences, Kwale (FUHSK) is a specialised federal university established in 2023, dedicated to medical education, health research and professional training.
371.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes in medicine and the health sciences.
371.c: It is located in Kwale, Delta State.

372.h: The Federal University of Health Sciences, Funtua is a specialised federal university established in 2023. It was set up with support from the Federal Government, the Katsina State Government and the Funtua community.
372.a: The university trains students in medicine and the health sciences. Its current priorities include completing its teaching hospital.
372.c: It is in Katsina State, with student services including a health centre, counselling, accommodation and a Student Affairs Division.
